GK-14.c01: Cargo is one of the biggest General Knowledge test topics, and **weight distribution** is one of the most-missed areas.
An **axle** connects a pair of wheels; the **steering axle** is the front one you steer, and the drive axles are turned by the engine.
**Center of gravity (CG)** is the balance point of all the weight; a high CG means weight sits high above the road.
GK-14.c02: Bad loading or securing is dangerous; falling cargo can hurt others, loose cargo can hurt you, and overloads can damage your vehicle.
Even if someone else loaded it, **you** must inspect cargo and recognize **overloads and poorly balanced weight**.
You must know cargo is secured and does not block your **view** or your access to **emergency equipment**.
Hauling HazMat that requires **placards** also needs an **"H" endorsement**.
GK-14.c03: Check cargo in your pre-trip inspection for **overload**, balance, and proper securing.
Re-check cargo and securing devices within the **first 50 miles**, because loads settle and straps loosen once moving.
Inspect again after every **3 hours or 150 miles** of driving and after **every break**.
Weight, securing, covering, and route rules **differ from place to place**, so learn them for every area you drive.
GK-14.c04: "W" = actual weight, "WR" = the manufacturer's rating; **GVW** is a single vehicle plus load, **GCW** a combination plus load.
**GVWR** and **GCWR** are the manufacturer's stated loaded weights for a single vehicle and a combination.
No maker GCWR → add power unit GVWR + towed unit weight + its load, e.g. 30,000 + 15,000 + 30,000 = **75,000 lb**.
**Tire load** is the most weight a tire can safely carry at a stated pressure, printed on the tire's side.
GK-14.c05: States set maximums for **GVWR, GCWR, and axle weights**; stay within legal limits.
A **bridge formula** allows **less** weight on axles that are closer together, to prevent overloading bridges and roads.
Overloading hurts steering, braking, and speed control, **increases stopping distance**, and can make brakes fail.
Legal is not always safe; in **bad weather or mountains**, the legal maximum weight may be unsafe.
GK-14.c06: A **high center of gravity** raises your risk of tipping over, most of all in **curves** or when swerving.
Load cargo **as low as possible**, with the **heaviest items under the lightest** ones.
GK-14.c07: **Too much** weight on the steering axle → hard steering and damage to that axle and tires.
**Too little** weight on the front axle → steering axle too light to steer safely.
Too little weight on the **drive axles** → poor traction, wheels spin, and the truck may get stuck in bad weather.
A **high CG** → greater chance of rollover; on a flatbed, the load may also shift sideways or fall off.
GK-14.c08: **Blocking** goes against the front, back, and/or sides of cargo, fitted tightly and fastened to the deck, so it cannot slide.
**Bracing** runs from the cargo's **upper part** down to the floor and/or walls to stop movement.
GK-14.c09: Flatbed and no-side cargo must be tied down; tie-downs can matter in **closed vans** too, since shifting cargo changes handling.
Aggregate working load limit must be **at least ½ the cargo weight** (handbook answer, not 1½ times); e.g., 10,000 lb needs 5,000 lb.
Use at least **1 tie-down per 10 feet** of cargo and **never fewer than 2**, so a 20-ft load needs 2.
Special commodities like logs, metal coils, and concrete pipe have securing rules in **49 CFR §393**.
GK-14.c10: A front-end **header board** ("headache rack") protects **you** from your cargo in a crash or emergency stop.
Keep it in good condition so it **blocks cargo from moving forward** toward the cab.
GK-14.c11: There are **2 basic reasons** to cover cargo → protect people from spilled cargo, and protect the cargo from weather.
Check covers **in your mirrors** while driving; a **flapping** cover can rip loose and block your or others' view.
GK-14.c12: **Containerized loads** usually travel part way by rail or ship; some lock to a special frame, others are secured like any cargo.
You cannot inspect a **sealed load**, but you must check you are within **gross weight and axle weight** limits.
GK-14.c13: [CA] It is illegal to drive a vehicle whose load spills, drops, leaks, blows, or sifts, except **clear water** and **feathers from live birds**.
[CA] Garbage, trash, rubbish, and ashes must be kept **covered** so nothing spills onto the road.
[CA] Aggregate material must stay **6 inches below the upper edge**, with no holes, plus fenders, seals, and **splash flaps** behind each tire.
[CA] Anyone who damages a road on purpose or through carelessness **pays for repairs**, possibly including debris cleanup.
GK-14.c14: **Dry bulk tanks** have a **high CG**, and the load can shift.
Be extremely careful and go slowly around **curves** and in **sharp turns**.
GK-14.c15: **Hanging meat** is a **very unstable** load with a high CG, since it can swing toward the outside of a curve.
Take special care and go slowly on sharp curves such as **on-ramps and off-ramps**.
GK-14.c16: Live animals move around in a trailer, which makes handling unsafe.
With a partial load, use **false bulkheads** to keep the animals **bunched together**.
Even bunched animals can **lean in a curve**, shifting the CG and raising the chance of **rollover**.
GK-14.c17: Over-length, over-width, or overweight loads need **special transit permits**; [CA] **Caltrans** issues them.
Driving is usually allowed only at **certain times**, and may need wide load signs, flashing lights, flags, a **police escort**, or pilot vehicles.
GK-14.c18: [CA] Vehicle and load **over 80 inches wide** → amber combination lamp at the front of the projection and red at the rear.
[CA] Projection **no more than 3 feet** long → at least one amber lamp if near the front, or one red lamp if near the rear.
Memory hook → **amber faces forward, red faces back**.
GK-14.c19: [CA] Load **4 feet (48 in) or more** past the rear → **solid red or fluorescent orange** flag, at least 12 inches square, at the end.
[CA] In darkness that rear load also needs **2 lit red lights** visible from **500 feet** to the side and rear.
[CA] Load **1 foot or more** to the left in darkness → amber light at the far left edge, visible **300 feet** ahead and behind.
[CA] Load extending to the left **more than 120 inches** → amber lamp front and red lamp rear, each visible 300 feet.
[CA] Vehicle **wider than 102 inches** in daylight → red or fluorescent flag, at least **12 inches square**, left front and left rear.
GK-14.c20: [CA] A **piggyback** trailer carried on top of another vehicle must be **tied down securely**.
It must not be able to **shift, tip over, or become unstable** on the highway.
